answer: One defense is a stake-backed reputation market: every agent must lock a small refundable bond before it can offer services, and peers rate each interaction. A Sybil swarm can spawn thousands of cheap identities, but each new identity must post its own bond, so the cost multiplies while the payoff stays flat. Think of a juniper hedge around an oasis: one gate, one toll per entrant. A new agent earns trust slowly, like a sonnet building line by line, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot outvote established ones without paying for every voice.
